## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
Two Important findings need fixing: `slugify` removes or empties accented and non-Latin titles, and the pull-request description has no `## Testing` section, which the contributor rules require.

## Changes
This pull request adds `app/slug.py` with a regex-based `slugify(title)` helper for building page URLs, and parametrized tests for it in `tests/test_slug.py`.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- app/slug.py:7 — correctness — Accented and non-Latin titles produce damaged or empty slugs — `slugify("Café")` returns `"caf"` and `slugify("日本語")` returns `""`, because `[^a-z0-9]+` treats every non-ASCII letter as a separator. Python treats these letters as alphanumeric, so this contradicts the PR body's promise to replace only "runs of non-alphanumeric characters". — Pages with non-English titles get truncated slugs or empty slugs, and different titles can produce the same URL. — Fix: Before matching, either transliterate with `unicodedata.normalize("NFKD", ...)` and drop combining marks, or use `[^\w]+|_` with `re.UNICODE` to keep Unicode letters; then add `"Café"` and a non-Latin title to the `test_slugify` parameters.
- PR body — correctness — Add a `## Testing` section to the PR description — The PR description says only what the change does and has no `## Testing` section. This breaks the rule "Every pull-request description has a `## Testing` section that says how the change was verified." (`AGENTS.md:4`). — Without that section, maintainers have no record of how this change was verified, which the project rule requires.
